description.value: The Armstrong branch of the Okanagan Regional Library is part of a 30-branch regional system serving the North Okanagan's small agricultural city of Armstrong. The branch offers free public computer and internet access, two reservable meeting/study rooms, and free car parking directly in front of the building. Its accessible, single-level facility with automatic doors and a wheelchair ramp makes it a practical indoor rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website at orl.bc.ca/hours-locations/armstrong is fully accessible and confirms this is an active public library branch. The website lists free car parking, computer/internet stations, meeting rooms, automatic doors, and a wheelchair ramp — but makes no mention of bike racks, water bottle refill stations, or washrooms, so those criteria remain null. Two discrepancies were found: the phone number on the website ((250) 546-8311) differs from the OSM tag (+1-250-838-6488), and the postcode on the website (V0E 1B1) differs from OSM (V4Y 0A2); website values are used per rule 12.
concerns: Phone number mismatch: OSM has +1-250-838-6488; website shows (250) 546-8311. Website value used.
Postcode mismatch: OSM has V4Y 0A2; website shows V0E 1B1. Website value used.
Category 'Attractions' is a poor fit for a public library branch; may warrant recategorization as a rest stop or service facility in the WWC directory.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The library is a legitimate cycling rest stop (free parking, internet access, accessible facility), but neither bike parking nor washrooms could be confirmed from the website, and two contact discrepancies (phone number and postcode) between OSM and the website need resolution before publishing.

provenance.category_correction_reason: A public library branch is not typically an attraction in the tourism sense; it functions more as a cyclist service stop (rest, connectivity, washrooms). However, no alternative WWC category was specified, so 'Attractions' is retained from the OSM record.
